name: Aluleth Funnels – Sales Funnel Builder & Order Bumps
author: aluleth

sections.description:
Aluleth Funnels takes your visitors from one page to the next: a sales or opt-in page, a checkout made for one offer, then a thank-you page. You see the whole funnel on a canvas, with how many people visit each step and how many go on.

The canvas

  • Every step of a funnel as a card with a picture of its page and three numbers, joined by arrows that show the share of people who go on (or buy).
  • Drag a new step from the list onto the canvas, or add one on an arrow with its + button. Drag the steps where you want them or move them with the arrow keys; zoom, fit, tidy up in a row, undo, and a small map of the funnel.
  • Click a step to open its settings beside the canvas. Everything also works without JavaScript.
  • The same steps as a table, for small screens and screen readers.

Ready-made funnels

  • 10 whole funnels to start from, each in its own look: a course launch, a video page, a free checklist, a webinar sign-up, a free guide with a small first offer, a physical product, a paid session, your store checkout, a monthly box and a digital download.
  • Every template brings all its pages (sales or opt-in page, checkout with its order bump, one-click offer, thank-you page) and puts the funnel on the canvas.
  • Made for the block editor and for Elementor, with their own blocks and widgets: every colour, size and text can be changed in the builder.
  • Preview each page on a desktop, tablet or phone size before importing, and choose the colours (one of 8 colour sets or your theme’s colours), the fonts and the store.
  • Each page can also be used alone: give any step the design of a page from another template, in the colours of your funnel.
  • The fonts come with the plugin and load from your own site (no font service). Texts in [brackets] and image places are there to be replaced; there are no invented reviews or numbers.

Get started, or switch from another plugin

  • A setup assistant (Aluleth › Get started): your store and the payment methods that take one-click offers, your page builder, then your first funnel. You open it from the empty Funnels list, the Plugins screen or the settings: it never takes over the admin, installs nothing and sends nothing. Every step can be skipped.
  • Import your funnels from CartFlows, FunnelKit or WPFunnels, even with that plugin switched off: their pages are copied in the same builder with their checkout, opt-in, next-step, offer and order parts swapped for ours, plus the products, coupon, order bumps, one-click offers and their paths. A check first says what each part becomes and what can’t come over. The originals, stats and orders stay where they are; imported funnels start switched off.

Steps are real pages

  • Each step is a page you edit with the block editor or Elementor (Elementor steps are real Elementor pages).
  • Blank layout without the theme’s menu and footer (fewer ways out of the funnel), or the theme’s layout if you prefer.
  • Blocks (and shortcodes for other builders): “Next step” button, opt-in form, the checkout, one-click offer buttons, order details, “Add to calendar” for a webinar or a call.
  • Addresses like /go/spring-course/; the start of the address can be changed.

Checkout for WooCommerce, FluentCart and Aluleth Commerce

  • A checkout step sells the products you choose (with quantities and an optional coupon), with the store’s own checkout: taxes, shipping, coupons and payment methods work as usual. Payment fields come from your payment gateways; card numbers never reach this plugin.
  • After payment the buyer goes to the next step of the funnel (usually the thank-you page), which shows what they ordered.
  • With several products, the buyer gets all of them or chooses one; the buyer can change the quantity if you allow it.
  • One or two columns, express pay buttons on or off, and for WooCommerce the fields of this checkout: last name, company, phone (required, optional or hidden) and the address only when something must be shipped.
  • WooCommerce: works with the Checkout block and the classic checkout, and with its order tables (HPOS).
  • Your store checkout: carts that are not in a funnel can use a funnel checkout too, with its order bump and thank-you page.

Order bumps

  • Up to 5 order bumps per checkout, each one more product with a tick box: shown together, in the order you choose. A bump adds its product, or replaces the products of the checkout (an upgrade or a bundle).
  • Each bump: at the store price, a percentage or an amount off, or a fixed price. Five looks (including your theme’s colours and the colours of the template) and three places (above the pay button, after the contact fields, in the order summary).
  • It is added to the order before payment, so it works with every payment method. The bump price only applies in its own checkout, one item at a time; prices are always worked out on your site, never taken from the browser.
  • See how often it is taken and what it added.

One-click upsell

  • Up to 10 one-click offers per funnel right after payment: the buyer clicks “Yes, add it to my order” and it is charged to the payment they just made, without filling in anything again.
  • Each answer can lead to its own step: “No thanks” can lead to a cheaper offer (a downsell) and buyers who can not be charged to another page, or everyone goes straight on.
  • FluentCart with PayPal: when the buyer pays with their PayPal account, PayPal asks them to keep it for your shop (FluentCart’s own PayPal support), and the offer is charged to it through FluentCart. Card buyers are never asked to make a PayPal account. The offer is a separate order, linked to the first one and refunded on its own.
  • Buyers who paid in a way that can not be charged again (card, cash on delivery, Paddle…) never see a dead end: they skip the offer page, and the canvas counts them as skipped. Funnels › Settings shows which of your payment methods work.
  • WooCommerce with WooCommerce PayPal Payments: the same, through PayPal Payments’ own connection to PayPal (your PayPal account must allow keeping buyers’ accounts, also called vaulting or reference transactions; the payment check tells you). The offer is a separate WooCommerce order, refunded on its own.
  • Stripe and WooPayments come in a next version.
  • Prices and tax: the offer is priced and taxed like the product in the buyer’s cart, at the address of the order just paid. A buyer who was tax exempt for that order (for example with a VAT number, in WooCommerce) is tax exempt for the offer too. The offer page shows what is charged, tax included. No shipping is added: a physical product offered after payment ships with the first order.

Opt-ins

  • The opt-in form makes the visitor a contact (with a consent tick box for marketing emails and an optional tag), then sends them to the next step.
  • A field robots fill in and a limit per connection keep spam out.

Numbers

  • Visits, people who went on, sign-ups, orders and revenue of every step, for the last 7 days, 30 days or 12 months.
  • A visit counts once per browser session and step. Bots, link previews and your own team are not counted.

Ad pixels

  • Meta (Facebook, Instagram), Google (Analytics 4 and Google Ads) and TikTok pixels on funnel pages only, set once for the site; a funnel can use its own pixels, or none.
  • Each pixel loads only after the visitor allows it in your cookie banner (any banner that uses the WP Consent API: Complianz, CookieYes, Cookiebot, iubenda…): Meta, TikTok and Google Ads need “marketing”, Google Analytics “statistics”. Google Consent Mode is set for you. Without a banner the pixels stay off, unless you say no visitor of your site needs one.
  • The funnel’s events in each platform’s words: page seen, sales page seen, sign-up, checkout, order bump added, purchase (once paid, with the order number as its id, sent once; each one-click offer is a purchase of its own).
  • You and your logged-in team, robots and link previews are never tracked. If your site already loads a pixel, choose “Already on my site” and only the funnel’s events are added.

Works with the other Aluleth plugins

  • Buyers and people who sign up become contacts, with the funnel on their timeline; Aluleth CRM can start automations from it.

Aluleth Funnels Pro, a separate plugin, adds more ready-made funnels (new ones with each update), makes every template for Bricks, Divi, Breakdance and Oxygen too, adds conditions to one-click offers and order bumps, A/B tests of any step (up to 4 versions, at the same address), full numbers of each funnel, and sends the purchases to Meta, Google and TikTok from your server too.

External services

Aluleth Funnels sends nothing to us and, with its settings as they are after install, contacts no outside service. Funnels, their numbers, contacts and funnel orders stay in your WordPress database. The services below are used only when you turn them on, or when a visitor clicks a link.

Ad pixels (off until you add them)

In Funnels › Settings › Tracking (or in one funnel’s settings) you can add the ids of your own ad accounts. Funnel pages then load the platform’s script in the visitor’s browser and send it the funnel’s events: page seen, sales page seen, sign-up, checkout started, order bump added and purchase once paid (with the order value, the currency, the ids, names, quantities and prices of the products, and an event id so a purchase is counted once). Nothing loads and nothing is sent before the visitor allows it in your cookie banner (WP Consent API): Meta and TikTok and Google Ads need “marketing”, Google Analytics needs “statistics”. Without a cookie banner the pixels stay off, unless you say no visitor of your site needs one.

  • Meta Pixel (Facebook, Instagram): script from connect.facebook.net. Terms, Privacy policy.
  • Google Analytics 4 and Google Ads: script from www.googletagmanager.com (gtag.js), with Google Consent Mode. Terms, Privacy policy.
  • TikTok Pixel: script from analytics.tiktok.com. Terms, Privacy policy.

Add to Google Calendar link

The thank-you page of a webinar or event funnel can show an “Add to Google Calendar” link. Nothing is sent until the visitor clicks it; the click opens calendar.google.com with the event’s title, date, description and place in the address. Terms, Privacy policy.

Payments

Checkouts and one-click offers are paid through your store plugin (WooCommerce, FluentCart or Aluleth Commerce) and the payment methods you set up there, like any other order of your store. Aluleth Funnels contacts no payment service itself.

Shared Aluleth screens

Aluleth Funnels comes with the screens shared by all Aluleth plugins (Aluleth › Settings and Aluleth › Connections). They are mostly used by Aluleth Forms and the other Aluleth plugins. None of the services below is contacted unless you paste your own key or address in one of these screens. With Aluleth Funnels alone, that is only when you click a “Save and check”, “Connect” or “Send a test” button there, and, once captcha keys are saved, when you open Aluleth › Settings › Security: it shows the service’s test check, which loads its script in your browser.

  • Mailchimp (*.api.mailchimp.com), email marketing. When you connect your account in Aluleth › Connections, your API key is sent to read your lists, tags and fields. Terms of use, Privacy policy.
  • Brevo (api.brevo.com), email marketing. Same use and data as Mailchimp. Terms of use, Privacy policy.
  • MailerLite (connect.mailerlite.com), email marketing. Same use and data. Terms of service, Privacy policy.
  • Kit (api.kit.com), email marketing. Same use and data. Terms of service, Privacy policy.
  • Mautic, marketing automation that you host yourself: the address of your own Mautic and its API user, sent only to that address. Mautic privacy policy.
  • Telegram (api.telegram.org), messaging. When you connect a bot, its token is sent to read the bot’s name and the chats that wrote to it. Terms of service, Privacy policy.
  • Discord (https://discord.com/api/webhooks/…; the discordapp.com, canary.discord.com and ptb.discord.com forms of the same address are accepted), chat. A message is posted to the channel webhook address you paste, and nowhere else. It is sent only when another Aluleth plugin sends an alert (for example, with Aluleth Forms, a new form entry with its answers and a link to it), or when you click “Send a test” (a sample message with no personal data). Aluleth Funnels alone sends no message to Discord. Terms of service, Privacy policy.
  • Slack (https://hooks.slack.com/services/…), chat. Same use and data as Discord, to the Slack webhook address you paste. Terms of service, Privacy policy.
  • Your own webhook addresses receive the same kind of message, only when another Aluleth plugin sends one or when you click “Send a test”.
  • Captcha services, in Aluleth › Settings › Security: “Save and check the keys” sends your secret key and a test answer to the service you chose, to tell you whether the keys work. Cloudflare Turnstile (challenges.cloudflare.com, for the test check and the key check): Terms of use, Privacy policy. hCaptcha (js.hcaptcha.com for the test check, api.hcaptcha.com): Terms of service, Privacy policy. Google reCAPTCHA (www.google.com/recaptcha, for the test check and the key check): Terms of service, Privacy policy. CleanTalk (moderate.cleantalk.org), a short test message with your access key: Terms of service, Privacy policy. These services check visitors only on the forms of Aluleth Forms; Aluleth Funnels adds no captcha to your pages.
  • PayPal: the Payments settings and the PayPal code are only used with Aluleth Forms; they are hidden and never run with Aluleth Funnels alone. User agreement, Privacy statement.

Privacy

Aluleth Funnels sends nothing to us. When you set ad pixels (Funnels › Settings › Tracking), funnel pages load the scripts of those platforms and send them the funnel’s events, but only after the visitor allows it in your cookie banner: Meta (https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/), Google (https://policies.google.com/privacy) and TikTok (https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/global/privacy-policy/en). Add them to your privacy policy and your cookie banner. The plugin keeps the visitor’s choice at payment with the funnel order (statistics and marketing, nothing else). Two short cookies of its own help: alfn_px (for the browser visit: purchases already sent, so none is sent twice) and alfn_lead (10 minutes: a sign-up to send on the next page). A one-click offer is charged by your store’s own payment code (for example FluentCart’s PayPal), with your payment provider, like any other payment of your store. Contacts and funnel orders stay in your WordPress database; the personal data export and erase tools …
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open the setup assistant from the Funnels screen (optional), or go to Aluleth › Funnels › New funnel and pick a template, import your funnels from another plugin, or start blank. Preview it, choose its colours, fonts, store and page builder, then import it.
  3. On the canvas, choose the product of the checkout step (and of the one-click offer), write your texts in the pages, then turn the funnel on.
sections.faq:
Do I need a store plugin (WooCommerce, FluentCart or Aluleth Commerce)?

Only to sell. Funnels that collect leads (opt-in steps) work without a store.

Can I bring my funnels from CartFlows, FunnelKit or WPFunnels?

Yes, in Funnels › New funnel › Import from another plugin. The import reads their data from your database (the other plugin can be on or off) and makes Aluleth funnels, switched off, with copies of the pages. Pages made with Bricks, Oxygen or Breakdance get our starter pages instead. Order bumps and offers of their Pro add-ons come over when their data can be read; anything that can’t is listed in the check.

Are funnel pages cached?

No. They ask page-cache plugins not to cache them, so every visitor gets their own checkout.

What does the plugin store about visitors?

A session cookie with the numbers of the funnel steps seen in this browser session (no identifier; it is deleted when the browser closes), to count each visit once. After an opt-in, a second session cookie, alfn_vis (signed), keeps the contact’s number and their answer to the opt-in question for this visit, so the next steps can use them. People who sign up or buy become contacts in your own database.

0.13.8

  • Aluleth Commerce as a store: checkout steps drawn from the step’s own cart (options and order bumps priced by the store), a “Your store checkout” step that replaces the Aluleth Commerce checkout page, paid and refunded orders counted in the funnel numbers, and a thank-you step that shows the bank details of bank transfer orders. One-click offers after payment are not available with Aluleth Commerce yet (they need saved payment methods).

0.13.7

  • Up to 5 order bumps per checkout and up to 10 one-click offers per funnel, and each answer to an offer (“no thanks”, payment that can not be taken) can lead to its own step, such as a downsell. An order bump can replace the products of its checkout (an upgrade or a bundle).
  • The answer to a one-click offer is also checked with a WordPress nonce.
  • The store checkout and thank-you output shown in step pages is escaped with an allowlist made for checkout forms.
  • The template buttons get the address of the next step through WordPress’s template output buffer.
  • Contact import files of the shared screens are plain CSV files in the plugin’s own folder of the uploads folder (wp-content/uploads/aluleth-funnels/imports), closed to web requests and deleted a week after the import.
  • Shared Aluleth core 0.18.8.

0.13.6

  • The setup assistant and the With AI tab say that AI funnels sell WooCommerce products and need WooCommerce; FluentCart funnels and funnels without a store start from a template or a blank funnel. Without WooCommerce, the AI choice of the setup assistant is off and says why.

0.13.5

  • WooCommerce one-click offers: a buyer who was tax exempt for the order just paid (for example with a VAT number) is tax exempt for the offer too: no tax on the offer page, the offer’s order or the payment. The offer’s order keeps the exemption when WooCommerce recalculates it.
  • WooCommerce one-click offers are priced as WooCommerce prices the product in the buyer’s cart, also with prices entered with tax for a buyer outside the shop’s country. When prices are shown before tax, the offer page also shows the total charged with its tax.

0.13.4

  • One-click offers are taxed like the product in your store (WooCommerce taxes and tax classes, FluentCart taxes) at the buyer’s address; when your shop shows prices before tax, the offer says so.

  • Answers to two offers recorded at the same moment are both kept; an order recorded twice at the same moment is told to other plugins once.
  • A buyer who declines an offer is never sent the “yes” way, even when something goes wrong while the answer is saved.
  • Sign-up and cart limits hold when many requests arrive at the same moment.
  • Order bump texts and offer notes are shortened by characters, not bytes; the plugin no longer needs the PHP mbstring extension. Contact import files of the shared screens can no longer be opened from their address on any server.

  • Every template brings all its pages (sales or opt-in page, checkout with its order bump, one-click offer, thank-you page) and puts the funnel on the canvas.
  • Made for the block editor and for Elementor, with their own blocks and widgets: every colour, size and text can be changed in the builder.
  • Preview each page on a desktop, tablet or phone size before importing, and choose the colours (one of 8 colour sets or your theme’s colours), the fonts and the store.
  • Each page can also be used alone: give any step the design of a page from another template, in the colours of your funnel.
  • The fonts come with the plugin and load from your own site (no font service). Texts in [brackets] and image places are there to be replaced; there are no invented reviews or numbers.

Get started, or switch from another plugin

  • A setup assistant (Aluleth › Get started): your store and the payment methods that take one-click offers, your page builder, then your first funnel. You open it from the empty Funnels list, the Plugins screen or the settings: it never takes over the admin, installs nothing and sends nothing. Every step can be skipped.
  • Import your funnels from CartFlows, FunnelKit or WPFunnels, even with that plugin switched off: their pages are copied in the same builder with their checkout, opt-in, next-step, offer and order parts swapped for ours, plus the products, coupon, order bumps, one-click offers and their paths. A check first says what each part becomes and what can’t come over. The originals, stats and orders stay where they are; imported funnels start switched off.

Steps are real pages

  • Each step is a page you edit with the block editor or Elementor (Elementor steps are real Elementor pages).
  • Blank layout without the theme’s menu and footer (fewer ways out of the funnel), or the theme’s layout if you prefer.
  • Blocks (and shortcodes for other builders): “Next step” button, opt-in form, the checkout, one-click offer buttons, order details, “Add to calendar” for a webinar or a call.
  • Addresses like /go/spring-course/; the start of the address can be changed.

Checkout for WooCommerce, FluentCart and Aluleth Commerce

  • A checkout step sells the products you choose (with quantities and an optional coupon), with the store’s own checkout: taxes, shipping, coupons and payment methods work as usual. Payment fields come from your payment gateways; card numbers never reach this plugin.
  • After payment the buyer goes to the next step of the funnel (usually the thank-you page), which shows what they ordered.
  • With several products, the buyer gets all of them or chooses one; the buyer can change the quantity if you allow it.
  • One or two columns, express pay buttons on or off, and for WooCommerce the fields of this checkout: last name, company, phone (required, optional or hidden) and the address only when something must be shipped.
  • WooCommerce: works with the Checkout block and the classic checkout, and with its order tables (HPOS).
  • Your store checkout: carts that are not in a funnel can use a funnel checkout too, with its order bump and thank-you page.

Order bumps

  • Up to 5 order bumps per checkout, each one more product with a tick box: shown together, in the order you choose. A bump adds its product, or replaces the products of the checkout (an upgrade or a bundle).
  • Each bump: at the store price, a percentage or an amount off, or a fixed price. Five looks (including your theme’s colours and the colours of the template) and three places (above the pay button, after the contact fields, in the order summary).
  • It is added to the order before payment, so it works with every payment method. The bump price only applies in its own checkout, one item at a time; prices are always worked out on your site, never taken from the browser.
  • See how often it is taken and what it added.

One-click upsell

  • Up to 10 one-click offers per funnel right after payment: the buyer clicks “Yes, add it to my order” and it is charged to the payment they just made, without filling in anything again.
  • Each answer can lead to its own step: “No thanks” can lead to a cheaper offer (a downsell) and buyers who can not be charged to another page, or everyone goes straight on.
  • FluentCart with PayPal: when the buyer pays with their PayPal account, PayPal asks them to keep it for your shop (FluentCart’s own PayPal support), and the offer is charged to it through FluentCart. Card buyers are never asked to make a PayPal account. The offer is a separate order, linked to the first one and refunded on its own.
  • Buyers who paid in a way that can not be charged again (card, cash on delivery, Paddle…) never see a dead end: they skip the offer page, and the canvas counts them as skipped. Funnels › Settings shows which of your payment methods work.
  • WooCommerce with WooCommerce PayPal Payments: the same, through PayPal Payments’ own connection to PayPal (your PayPal account must allow keeping buyers’ accounts, also called vaulting or reference transactions; the payment check tells you). The offer is a separate WooCommerce order, refunded on its own.
  • Stripe and WooPayments come in a next version.
  • Prices and tax: the offer is priced and taxed like the product in the buyer’s cart, at the address of the order just paid. A buyer who was tax exempt for that order (for example with a VAT number, in WooCommerce) is tax exempt for the offer too. The offer page shows what is charged, tax included. No shipping is added: a physical product offered after payment ships with the first order.

Opt-ins

  • The opt-in form makes the visitor a contact (with a consent tick box for marketing emails and an optional tag), then sends them to the next step.
  • A field robots fill in and a limit per connection keep spam out.

Numbers

  • Visits, people who went on, sign-ups, orders and revenue of every step, for the last 7 days, 30 days or 12 months.
  • A visit counts once per browser session and step. Bots, link previews and your own team are not counted.

Ad pixels

  • Meta (Facebook, Instagram), Google (Analytics 4 and Google Ads) and TikTok pixels on funnel pages only, set once for the site; a funnel can use its own pixels, or none.
  • Each pixel loads only after the visitor allows it in your cookie banner (any banner that uses the WP Consent API: Complianz, CookieYes, Cookiebot, iubenda…): Meta, TikTok and Google Ads need “marketing”, Google Analytics “statistics”. Google Consent Mode is set for you. Without a banner the pixels stay off, unless you say no visitor of your site needs one.
  • The funnel’s events in each platform’s words: page seen, sales page seen, sign-up, checkout, order bump added, purchase (once paid, with the order number as its id, sent once; each one-click offer is a purchase of its own).
  • You and your logged-in team, robots and link previews are never tracked. If your site already loads a pixel, choose “Already on my site” and only the funnel’s events are added.

Works with the other Aluleth plugins

  • Buyers and people who sign up become contacts, with the funnel on their timeline; Aluleth CRM can start automations from it.

Aluleth Funnels Pro, a separate plugin, adds more ready-made funnels (new ones with each update), makes every template for Bricks, Divi, Breakdance and Oxygen too, adds conditions to one-click offers and order bumps, A/B tests of any step (up to 4 versions, at the same address), full numbers of each funnel, and sends the purchases to Meta, Google and TikTok from your server too.

External services

Aluleth Funnels sends nothing to us and, with its settings as they are after install, contacts no outside service. Funnels, their numbers, contacts and funnel orders stay in your WordPress database. The services below are used only when you turn them on, or when a visitor clicks a link.

Ad pixels (off until you add them)

In Funnels › Settings › Tracking (or in one funnel’s settings) you can add the ids of your own ad accounts. Funnel pages then load the platform’s script in the visitor’s browser and send it the funnel’s events: page seen, sales page seen, sign-up, checkout started, order bump added and purchase once paid (with the order value, the currency, the ids, names, quantities and prices of the products, and an event id so a purchase is counted once). Nothing loads and nothing is sent before the visitor allows it in your cookie banner (WP Consent API): Meta and TikTok and Google Ads need “marketing”, Google Analytics needs “statistics”. Without a cookie banner the pixels stay off, unless you say no visitor of your site needs one.

  • Meta Pixel (Facebook, Instagram): script from connect.facebook.net. Terms, Privacy policy.
  • Google Analytics 4 and Google Ads: script from www.googletagmanager.com (gtag.js), with Google Consent Mode. Terms, Privacy policy.
  • TikTok Pixel: script from analytics.tiktok.com. Terms, Privacy policy.

Add to Google Calendar link

The thank-you page of a webinar or event funnel can show an “Add to Google Calendar” link. Nothing is sent until the visitor clicks it; the click opens calendar.google.com with the event’s title, date, description and place in the address. Terms, Privacy policy.

Payments

Checkouts and one-click offers are paid through your store plugin (WooCommerce, FluentCart or Aluleth Commerce) and the payment methods you set up there, like any other order of your store. Aluleth Funnels contacts no payment service itself.

Shared Aluleth screens

Aluleth Funnels comes with the screens shared by all Aluleth plugins (Aluleth › Settings and Aluleth › Connections). They are mostly used by Aluleth Forms and the other Aluleth plugins. None of the services below is contacted unless you paste your own key or address in one of these screens. With Aluleth Funnels alone, that is only when you click a “Save and check”, “Connect” or “Send a test” button there, and, once captcha keys are saved, when you open Aluleth › Settings › Security: it shows the service’s test check, which loads its script in your browser.

  • Mailchimp (*.api.mailchimp.com), email marketing. When you connect your account in Aluleth › Connections, your API key is sent to read your lists, tags and fields. Terms of use, Privacy policy.
  • Brevo (api.brevo.com), email marketing. Same use and data as Mailchimp. Terms of use, Privacy policy.
  • MailerLite (connect.mailerlite.com), email marketing. Same use and data. Terms of service, Privacy policy.
  • Kit (api.kit.com), email marketing. Same use and data. Terms of service, Privacy policy.
  • Mautic, marketing automation that you host yourself: the address of your own Mautic and its API user, sent only to that address. Mautic privacy policy.
  • Telegram (api.telegram.org), messaging. When you connect a bot, its token is sent to read the bot’s name and the chats that wrote to it. Terms of service, Privacy policy.
  • Discord (https://discord.com/api/webhooks/…; the discordapp.com, canary.discord.com and ptb.discord.com forms of the same address are accepted), chat. A message is posted to the channel webhook address you paste, and nowhere else. It is sent only when another Aluleth plugin sends an alert (for example, with Aluleth Forms, a new form entry with its answers and a link to it), or when you click “Send a test” (a sample message with no personal data). Aluleth Funnels alone sends no message to Discord. Terms of service, Privacy policy.
  • Slack (https://hooks.slack.com/services/…), chat. Same use and data as Discord, to the Slack webhook address you paste. Terms of service, Privacy policy.
  • Your own webhook addresses receive the same kind of message, only when another Aluleth plugin sends one or when you click “Send a test”.
  • Captcha services, in Aluleth › Settings › Security: “Save and check the keys” sends your secret key and a test answer to the service you chose, to tell you whether the keys work. Cloudflare Turnstile (challenges.cloudflare.com, for the test check and the key check): Terms of use, Privacy policy. hCaptcha (js.hcaptcha.com for the test check, api.hcaptcha.com): Terms of service, Privacy policy. Google reCAPTCHA (www.google.com/recaptcha, for the test check and the key check): Terms of service, Privacy policy. CleanTalk (moderate.cleantalk.org), a short test message with your access key: Terms of service, Privacy policy. These services check visitors only on the forms of Aluleth Forms; Aluleth Funnels adds no captcha to your pages.
  • PayPal: the Payments settings and the PayPal code are only used with Aluleth Forms; they are hidden and never run with Aluleth Funnels alone. User agreement, Privacy statement.

Privacy

Aluleth Funnels sends nothing to us. When you set ad pixels (Funnels › Settings › Tracking), funnel pages load the scripts of those platforms and send them the funnel’s events, but only after the visitor allows it in your cookie banner: Meta (https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/), Google (https://policies.google.com/privacy) and TikTok (https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/global/privacy-policy/en). Add them to your privacy policy and your cookie banner. The plugin keeps the visitor’s choice at payment with the funnel order (statistics and marketing, nothing else). Two short cookies of its own help: alfn_px (for the browser visit: purchases already sent, so none is sent twice) and alfn_lead (10 minutes: a sign-up to send on the next page). A one-click offer is charged by your store’s own payment code (for example FluentCart’s PayPal), with your payment provider, like any other payment of your store. Contacts and funnel orders stay in your WordPress database; the personal data export and erase tools …
